column_lineage.transformation: CASE WHEN pm.paid_date IS NULL THEN 'N' ELSE 'Y' END

summary: This job extracts premium instalment records from the billing system, removes exact duplicate rows, and computes a binary payment status flag to populate the staging premiums table for downstream financial processing.
risk_notes: De-duplication via `SELECT DISTINCT`: If `amount` is read into PySpark as `DoubleType` instead of `DecimalType`, floating-point representation differences can cause `.distinct()` to fail to collapse rows that T-SQL considered duplicate.

Null evaluation in `CASE WHEN pm.paid_date IS NULL`: Implicit string-to-date conversion errors during PySpark ingestion can turn malformed dates into `NULL`, incorrectly triggering the 'N' branch of `paid_flag`.

Schema inference on `amount`: T-SQL `SELECT INTO` preserves exact source column data types (e.g., `DECIMAL(18,2)`), whereas PySpark reader defaults might infer `DecimalType(38,18)` or floating-point types, causing precision mismatches in the lakehouse schema.
